title: Profit Metro Review 2026: Legit or Scam?
description: Profit Metro scam or legit? Its site says it only connects you to brokers it does not name, and gives both $250 and €250 deposits. Check this first.
author: Olivia Bennett
excerpt: Profit Metro scam or legit? Its site says it only connects you to brokers it does not name, and gives both $250 and €250 deposits. Check this first.
content:
Profit Metro is presented on meteor-profit.com as an AI trading software. The site describes itself as a service that connects users with trading service providers, and says it does not offer direct trading services itself.

The site's disclaimer says it connects crypto traders with brokers offering crypto, stocks, forex and CFDs, and that it cannot promise results. Those are the site's own statements, and we attribute them to it.

This review uses only what meteor-profit.com says. Claims come from that source and are attributed to it.

Profit Metro Explained: What the Source Says

According to the site, Profit Metro uses six indicators to scan the market and offers two modes: manual trading with alerts, and an automated mode that trades on the user's settings.

The site says the platform is web-based, needs no installation, and can be used on Windows, macOS, iOS and Android. It describes its AI as built on GPT-based systems, which the site does not explain further.

Everything in this table comes from the source. Where the source is silent, the table says so.

Platform Overview

Category Description
Platform Type AI trading software that connects users with brokers, per the site
Minimum Deposit The site gives $250 in its highlights and in the steps, and €250 in one FAQ answer. The currencies disagree

Profit Metro: Where the Source Stands Up, Where It Doesn’t

Here is what the source offers, and what it does not back up.

What Profit Metro states about itself:

  • The site states the sign-up is free and that withdrawal fees are free.
  • Two trading modes are described, manual and automatic, and the site says both can be changed at any time.
  • The disclaimer says the site cannot promise results or take responsibility for losses, and advises users to choose brokers carefully.
  • Encryption and privacy protection are described on the site.

Where Profit Metro Falls Short:

  • The deposit amount is inconsistent: $250 on the homepage and in the steps, €250 in one FAQ answer.
  • The brokers the site connects users with are not named, so the party holding funds cannot be identified from the site.
  • The site gives a 4.88 rating and claims fast execution at 0.01 seconds ahead of the market, with no source for either.
  • The site claims profits go straight to your bank account without cuts. It does not explain how or when a profit is paid.
  • No operator, regulator or licence is named.

The site's own disclaimer says it connects you with brokers and does not trade for you. Confirm who holds your money before you rely on any claim on the page.

What the Source Describes for Profit Metro

The site says it scans the market with six indicators and sends real-time alerts. In automatic mode, it says the system places trades on the user's settings.

The site says that after registration, your details are passed to a trusted provider to confirm the account, and that you are then matched with a broker. It does not name that provider or the broker.

Getting Set Up: The Steps the Source Describes

This is the sign-up route as the Profit Metro source lays it out. We did not open an account to check it.

1. Register

Sign up with a simple form. The site says it takes a few minutes and costs nothing.

2. Fund

The site says you need at least $250 to start. One FAQ answer says €250, so confirm the amount and currency before you deposit.

3. Invest

Choose manual or automatic mode from the Begin Trading button. The site says the process takes a few clicks.

After you register, the site says a trusted provider verifies your details and a broker is matched to your account. Ask who that broker is before you deposit.

What Profit Metro Costs: What the Source Says and Leaves Out

The site says there are no fees for registration, the platform or transactions, and that withdrawal fees are free.

The deposit amount is stated in both dollars and euros. The broker's own charges are not shown on the site.

Before you deposit, check these in writing:

  • The broker's spread or commission on each trade.
  • The deposit amount and currency confirmed in writing.
  • Any withdrawal, currency conversion or account maintenance charge at the broker.
  • How long a withdrawal takes once it is requested.

A site that says it charges no fees still sends you to a broker. Confirm the broker's costs before depositing.

What Profit Metro Covers

The site says the platform covers crypto, and its disclaimer mentions stocks, forex and CFDs through the connected brokers.

  • Cryptocurrencies, named as the main market.
  • Stocks, forex and CFDs, mentioned in the disclaimer through the brokers.
  • No full instrument list is given.

Check the instruments your broker offers before depositing, since the site does not list them.

Discover More

Is Profit Metro Legit?

The site says it aims to recommend legit and regulated firms, but states that the choice is the user's. The firms are not named.

The site describes encryption and a privacy policy. These are its own statements and were not checked.

What we could and could not confirm from the source:

  • The operator behind Meteor Profit: not named.
  • The regulator and licence of any broker it connects to: not named.
  • The 4.88 rating: no source given.
  • The claim of 0.01 second execution: no source given.

Checks you can run yourself:

  • Ask in writing which broker you would be connected to, and check that broker on its regulator's register.
  • Confirm the deposit amount and currency before you send money.
  • Search the name Meteor Profit for independent complaints and reviews, and read them with care.
  • Look up when the domain was registered, since a new domain deserves extra care.
  • Test a withdrawal with a small amount before you add more funds.

A site that connects users with brokers is not itself the regulated party. This section is general information, not legal or financial advice.

Learn More

Mistakes Worth Avoiding with Profit Metro

Assuming the site holds your money.

The site connects you with brokers. Ask which broker holds your funds.

Depositing without checking the amount.

The site gives $250 and €250. Confirm the figure first.

Relying on the 4.88 rating and the speed claim.

Neither is sourced on the site.

Learn More

A Quick Checklist Before You Deposit

Run through this before you send any money.

  • The broker you would be matched with named and checked on its regulator's register.
  • The deposit amount and currency confirmed in writing.
  • Broker charges, spreads and withdrawal terms obtained.
  • The operator behind the site identified.
  • A small test withdrawal completed before you add more funds.
Explore Profit Metro

Who Profit Metro May Suit, and Who Should Look Elsewhere

Profit Metro may suit someone who understands that the site hands them to a broker, and who will check that broker before depositing.

It is a poor fit for anyone who needs a named operator, a named broker and a regulator before sending money.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Profit Metro legit or a scam?

We could not confirm it. The site connects users with brokers it does not name, and it gives two different deposit amounts.

Is Profit Metro a scam?

We cannot say either way. Check the broker you would be matched with, and test a small withdrawal before you add more funds.

What is the Profit Metro minimum deposit?

The site says $250 in one place and €250 in another. Confirm the amount in writing.

Does Profit Metro charge fees?

The site says there are no fees for registration, the platform or transactions. Broker charges are not shown.

Is Profit Metro available in my country?

The site says all countries except the USA.

Does Profit Metro guarantee profits?

No. The site's disclaimer says it cannot promise specific results or take responsibility for losses.

Where We Land on Profit Metro

Profit Metro presents an AI trading tool that connects users with brokers. Its site gives no operator, no broker name and no regulator, and its deposit amount is stated in two currencies.

If you still want to look further, confirm the broker and its regulator first, get the deposit amount and charges in writing, and test a withdrawal before you add more funds.
